Sansi. 1,000: Pakistan'; Saxena & Borin 2008 Lesser-Known Languages of South Asia table listing).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Glottolog: only reference = Grierson 1922 (med = wordlist_or_less, 12 pp.), 'Comments on subclassification: Grierson 1922: 121-142'. Wikipedia: Kabutra 'almost identical to neighboring Sansi', unwritten; Kunri, Nara Dhoro, Umerkot; 1,000 speakers (1998).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1922. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. XI: Gipsy Languages. Calcutta: Superintendent Government Printing. Nat / Nati (Baisiya) section pp. 121-142 (the pages Glottolog cites for kabu1254; Hammarström's hh.bib maps 'Nati-Baisiya = Kabutra [kbu]').
sources.note: Silent. pp. 121-123 say 'there is no such dialect as Nati. The various clans classed together under the head of Nats speak the dialect of their neighbours... they have a professional argot' (United Provinces: Mainpuri, Etawah, Bijnor, Rampur), then argot word-disguise devices and Prodigal Son specimens; no accent/stress/tone/pronunciation remark anywhere in pp. 121-142 (grep = 0 hits). Only accent remark in the volume is the survey-wide transliteration note: 'When it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used.'
